title: Exposure Funnel Composer + Metrics Accordion Prototype for Nonlinear Rollouts
creator: Ava Chen
description: High-level: Prototype a novel composer and run-time inspector for 'nonlinear' rollouts — sequences that mix percentage ramps, cohort gates, and shadow lanes — focused on making risk visible and creating a low-friction rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Designer-created Figma prototype for composer canvas that supports: percentage ramps, cohort selection, shadow lanes, and a collapsible Metrics Accordion for run-time signals
Prototype includes a validation overlay that surfaces confidence bands and a quick rollback preview modal
PM and SRE sign-off that the metrics surfaced (latency P50/P95, error rate, model divergence, cost delta) map to alerting signals used by the runtime team
Usability test: 6 engineers/PMs can complete a canary+shadow setup and trigger a rollback preview within 6 minutes on first run
design_notes: Motivation: existing linear traffic-split flows assume monotonic ramps; many customers require branching exposures (e.g., 10% geo A, 5% cohort B, 100% shadow of new model) that are hard to author and reason about
Composer pattern: canvas + lanes + connectors. Lanes represent exposure channels (active, shadow, fallback). Connectors show traffic flow and allow quick swaps.

Metrics Accordion: a collapsible panel attached to each lane showing primary signals, deltas vs baseline, and a small sparkline timeline. Accordion rows have an embedded confidence indicator (green/yellow/red) and a tooltip explaining the statistical heuristic used.

Rollback preview: speculative simulation that shows expected user-facing impact (requests diverted, expected cost delta) and highlights which lanes will be affected by a snapback. Not a live action — preview only.
Accessibility: keyboard-first composer navigation and aria-labeled controls for lane actions. Color semantics paired with icons for color-blind users.
Trade-offs: detailed telemetry increases cognitive load; default collapsed state for Metrics Accordion with a prominent summary chip reduces noise. Advanced mode expands detailed signals.
decisions: Use a lane-first mental model rather than segment-first to simplify drag-and-drop composition for non-engineers
Metrics Accordion will surface a fixed set of 4 signals by default (P50 latency, P95 latency, error rate, relative token cost) with an option to add custom signals via a plus menu
Rollback preview will be read-only and require a second explicit confirmation in the runtime playbook to execute a rollback
Simulation uses historical traffic shape sampling from the last 7 days to estimate user impact (SRE asked for a 7-day window)
next_steps: Iterate Figma prototype (v2) to include the compact summary chip and advanced toggle (due 2026-03-15)
Align with runtime on signal mappings and API contract for metrics (owner: Diego)
Build a lightweight usability test script and recruit participants from infra, core-API, and a power PM (target date 2026-03-20)
Create a design handoff package for engineering including component token specs, behaviour matrix, and accessibility checklist
reviewers_feedback: Priya Kapoor (PM): Likes the lane-first model; asked for clearer language around what happens to active requests during a rollback
Samir Patel (SRE): Requested that error-rate signal be accompanied by a correlated request-count and suggested a 'confidence margin' indicator for small-sample cohorts
Lena Hoff (Engineer - runtime): Concerned about attaching heavy queries to the live composer; proposed an explicit 'Refresh metrics' button and backend throttling

2026-03-09 Priya Kapoor: PM review — asked for user-flow where customer can 'dry-run' a rollback without affecting live traffic. Design should make it explicit that preview is non-destructive.
